solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Senior Conservative leaders, arse-like, get strong booze

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
the rump is the backside, so rump-like, made into an adjective

explanation.surface: Tory grandees behaving like backsides while getting drunk on strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUMPY is rough, strong farmhouse cider from the West Country of England. RUMPY is a made-up adjective, typical of Private Eye's crude humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a potent unfiltered cider, so it is an example of alcoholic drink with a high kick.

clue.text: Bill's cocaine drug dose

blocks.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
a hit is a single dose of a drug

explanation.surface: Somebody named Bill owns a stash of cocaine and a dose of some drug.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bill's" reads as a man's possession; it is the definition, with 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short written note of money owed, such as a restaurant bill or voucher.

clue.text: Run around with nothing on and frig about? That's common

indicators.note: to move around is to change position, so the letters get rearranged
to turn about is to face the opposite way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O
both are crude slang for having sex

explanation.surface: Someone streaking naked and messing about, which the speaker sneers at as vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frig about' suggests idle messing around, but 'frig' is a crude verb for sex and 'about' turns it round. 'Common' here means lowly, the opposite of royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of common birth means being not of the royal family, so the negative adjective matches ordinary, low status.

clue.text: Babe possibly associated with leader and journalist? Perverse!

blocks.note: Babe is the talking piglet of the 1995 film, so an example of this animal
the head is the leader of a school or group
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman seen with a party leader and a reporter, which someone finds scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babe' suggests a glamorous young woman, but it is the film pig; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stubbornly contrary and obstinate is described as perverse, holding to a view against all reason.

clue.text: Boobs tip: needing lifts

blocks.note: to cock something is to tilt or tip it, as with a hat
ups are raises or lifts

explanation.surface: A beauty tip about breasts that need surgical lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boobs' reads as breasts; it means blunders. COCK-UP is British slang for a botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British informal for a silly mistake, and a cock-up is a cruder slang word for the same blunder.

clue.text: Take place with firm uplifted arse

indicators.note: lifted upwards in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
an arse is a contemptible person, as is a cur

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery on a firm, lifted backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm uplifted arse' reads as a toned bottom; 'arse' is instead an insult for a despicable person, and only 'firm' is uplifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen, so the verb means an event comes about.

clue.text: Ken, complete smartarse

blocks.note: ken is a Scots verb meaning to be aware of or understand
complete means whole, the entire amount

explanation.surface: Someone named Ken is dismissed as an utter show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name; it is the Scots verb for knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartarse is a person who shows off supposed cleverness, which is exactly what a conceited expert on everything does.

clue.text: For each preferred charge, execute!

blocks.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a pet project or pet subject is a favoured one
a rate is a fee or charge

explanation.surface: A command to put someone to death for each favoured criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' suggests killing; here it means carry out, as one carries out a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out a deed, especially a crime or blunder, is to commit or perform it.

clue.text: "Useless wanker's lost heart!" rejoinder

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word is dropped
something useless is broken or no good, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, including the S
the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: A retort shouted at a feeble idiot who has lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted insult is the fodder, not a speech; drop the middle K and rearrange the six remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rejoinder is a quick reply or retort, so a response to what has been said.

clue.text: Republican ball hosted by jackass military leader is 'a gas'

indicators.note: a guest who is hosted is taken in, so these letters sit inside the others

blocks.note: a nit is a fool, like a jackass
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a ball is round like the letter O
GEN is the abbreviation for general

explanation.surface: An idiotic general throws a Republican ball, which is described as great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A gas' is slang for a good time; the quotes hide its literal meaning, a chemical gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a colourless element making up most of the air, so it is one example of a gas.

clue.text: Chain and ball is about right for church groups

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length
a ball is round like the letter O
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A ball and chain seems a fitting device for keeping church groups in line.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old British unit of length, 22 yards, abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Choirs are groups of singers who perform in churches, leading hymns in services.

clue.text: Russian army campaign avoiding troop casualties? Could be rawer by far in gutless crusade

definitions.text: Russian army campaign avoiding troop casualties?

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged
without guts means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, all ten letters
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Russian military crusade that spares soldiers yet might be far more brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as descriptive: a campaign run by hackers kills no troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Attacks on computer networks are a form of conflict that inflicts damage without soldiers dying, which Russia is accused of waging.

clue.text: 'Rock bird', say, overturned ancient monument

indicators.note: turned over in a down entry means the letters read upwards, in reverse

blocks.note: a rock is a stone
a hen is a female bird
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A monument to a 'rock bird' has been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'Rock bird' carry no wordplay; only 'say' is overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain in England, a famous example of an old landmark.

clue.text: Indifferent when Trump's head stuck in concrete

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the opening letter is kept
something stuck in something else is lodged inside it

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
concrete in the sense of firm and substantial

explanation.surface: Someone is unmoved at the prospect of the president's head set in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' reads as the building material; it is the adjective meaning firm. The T goes after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive and showing little emotion, which is close to unconcerned or unmoved.

clue.text: Rudeness from Blair, somehow uninteresting

indicators.note: somehow means in some unstated way, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: the former Prime Minister's name taken as written
a dry subject is dull

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's crudeness is, oddly, dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator sits after the name it rearranges and before the adjective, so it belongs only to Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is coarse, bawdy humour, a kind of vulgar language or behaviour.

clue.text: Drunk a little – hazardous point for a motorist

blocks.note: blind drunk; blind alone is slang for very drunk
a spot is a small amount, as in a spot of tea

explanation.surface: Being slightly drunk is dangerous for a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a drink-driving warning; 'Drunk a little' splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The area a driver cannot see in mirrors is a well-known danger when changing lanes.

clue.text: Elected Trump having dumped politician: "Red oddball, unwelcome guest"

indicators.note: to dump something is to get rid of it, so those letters are removed
an oddball is strange and eccentric, so the letters are put in a peculiar order

blocks.note: a candidate who is elected is in
taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly elected Trump, having got rid of a politician, calls him a communist weirdo and an unwanted visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase looks like a Trump insult, but 'oddball' works on 'Red' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is someone who enters where they are not wanted, like an uninvited visitor.

clue.text: Upper class given devious Rupert's protection – a breach

indicators.note: a devious route twists about, so the letters are rearranged
a protector shelters what it guards, so one piece is kept safe inside another

blocks.note: the name as written, without the 's
U is the British shorthand for upper class

explanation.surface: Posh people sheltered by crafty Rupert Murdoch amounts to a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye's Rupert is Rupert Murdoch, the media owner. U for upper class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture is a break or split, whether in a pipe, a body wall or a relationship.

clue.text: Big city has time, er, for lawless Trump supporter?

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, a big Brazilian city
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city makes time for a lawless supporter of Trump, with a hesitant 'er'.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' reads as a hesitation but is literal letters. The question mark flags the definition as an example: the Capitol rioters of 6 January 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who stormed the US Capitol in 2021 were violent disorderly protesters, a notorious instance.

clue.text: Prompt, visible, audible

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: something visible can be seen, within view

explanation.surface: Three adjectives in a row, like a checklist for a well-run alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective in a list, but it is the verb meaning to urge on.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone to act is to stir or provoke them into doing it.

clue.text: Politician loses head after fashionable coffee alternative

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped
after means following, so this piece sits below the next one in the down entry

blocks.note: chic means stylish
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician gets decapitated after some trendy coffee substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: Politician comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because 'after' puts it below the trendy piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasted, ground chicory root is brewed as a substitute for or addition to coffee.

clue.text: Chiropody Hans almost botched causing unwarranted ill feeling

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off
something botched is badly bungled, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A foot doctor called Hans makes a mess of treatment and leaves a patient aggrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill feeling' suggests resentment; read literally it is feeling ill, and 'unwarranted' makes it imagined illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypochondria is excessive worry about being sick when there is no real medical cause.

clue.text: 'Green stuff' element of Dacre's salary

indicators.note: an element is a part of a larger whole, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively across the end of the name and start of the next word

explanation.surface: Money makes up part of a newspaper editor's pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Dacre was the long-serving editor of the Daily Mail. 'Green stuff' suggests money, but it is a salad plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a small leafy salad plant, literally a green vegetable.

clue.text: Hot place – climax of sexual relations needs to be taken outside

indicators.note: a climax is the final peak, so only the last letter is kept
the second piece must be taken around the first, holding it inside

blocks.note: kin are relatives
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Things get steamy as sex has to happen outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climax of sexual relations' reads as one phrase; it splits into 'climax of sexual' and 'relations', which goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is an oven for firing pottery or bricks at very high temperatures.

clue.text: Cover one nipple, initially  – fast!

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is kept

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the opening letter of the word
fast in the sense of firm and secure, as in hold fast

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to cover up a nipple quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' reads as hiding the nipple; it is the insurance sense. 'Fast' looks like speed but means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out cover on a house or car means buying an insurance policy to protect it.

clue.text: Joy, finally awake, gets out of bed with frightful hairdo – date leaves

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is kept
whatever leaves goes away, so those letters are removed
frightful means dreadful and messy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
someone out of bed is up
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Joy finally wakes and gets up with awful bed hair, while her date walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy' looks like a woman's name; it is the definition, and 'finally awake' takes only the end of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is an intense feeling of happiness and excitement, a strong form of delight.

clue.text: Openings of Russia's exhausted lines result in defeat

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
lines of poetry are verse

explanation.surface: Russia's worn-out front lines lead to a military loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests a battle front; it means lines of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or military loss, the noun used for a battlefield failure.

clue.text: Lockdown advice: government initially suspending

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the Covid instruction was to remain at home
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The government is set to drop its Covid lockdown advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspending' reads as the government ending the rules; it is the definition, the legal sense of halting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay an execution or proceedings is to postpone or halt them, a legal usage.
